titulo: Never Kill the Big Yellow Spider in Your Garden
titulos_alternativos: If You See This Yellow Spider in Your Garden, Do NOT Kill It
The "Writing Spider" in Your Garden Is Not Writing Your Name
descripcion:
It is a warm morning at the end of summer. You step outside to water the tomatoes, and you almost walk face first into a huge web. In the middle hangs the biggest spider you have ever seen in your yard: bright yellow and black, with a strange white zigzag running through the web. Your first thought is to grab a stick. Don't.

The yellow garden spider (Argiope aurantia), also called the writing spider, zipper spider or corn spider, is one of the hardest working pest hunters in your garden. Here is how her web works, how she hunts, why her tiny males die during mating, what that famous zigzag might really be for, and the truth about the old Southern story that says she can write your name.
